Subject to rules.normal: 9514 records carry NORM, but 445 of them also carry another diagnostic statement and 37 also carry AFIB -- those are disqualified / reported as ambiguous rather than accepted.

SCP diagnostic statement "left ventricular hypertrophy" (diagnostic_class HYP, diagnostic_subclass LVH). A diagnostic-level LVH assertion, not a voltage-criterion observation. 2132 records.

"Voltage criteria (QRS) for left ventricular hypertrophy". VERIFIED from scp_statements.csv: this is a FORM statement (form=1, diagnostic=NaN, no diagnostic_class) -- it records a voltage measurement, not an LVH diagnosis. PTB-XL's own annotators kept it distinct from LVH. The project rules explicitly forbid mapping "nonspecific voltage abnormalities" to LVH. 875 records. Flip to ACCEPT/LVH only if you decide voltage criteria alone should count -- and document that choice in your thesis if you do.

reason: SNOMED-CT 55827005 occurs in 5384 Chapman/Ningbo records (12% of the database) but is NOT defined in the shipped ConditionNames_SNOMED-CT.csv. EMPIRICAL INVESTIGATION (see README section 6). Signal-level testing indicates this code IS left ventricular hypertrophy: * Sokolow-Lyon voltage, measured from the waveforms: median 3.73 mV with 63.6% exceeding the 3.5 mV LVH threshold. PTB-XL's own diagnostic LVH statement scores 3.59 mV / 53.8% -- i.e. these records are indistinguishable from confirmed LVH annotated by a different institution in a different country. * Two independent control groups (Chapman sinus-rhythm-only, PTB-XL NORM) both sit at ~2.2 mV / ~3%, cross-validating the measurement. * Confounder "sick older patients" excluded: comorbidity-matched flutter patients without either LVH code score 2.22 mV / 8.8%. * Confounder "LBBB" excluded: QRS duration 70 ms, identical to normals (70 ms) and LVH (74 ms), versus 148 ms for confirmed CLBBB. DECISION: the records are nevertheless EXCLUDED ENTIRELY, because the evidence is behavioural rather than documentary -- the distribution still does not define the code, and no clinician has signed it off. EXCLUDE_RECORD (not EXCLUDE_UNCERTAIN) is used deliberately: leaving these records in the cohort under some other label would silently assert LVH=0 on ~370 recordings that most likely DO have LVH, which would train the LVH head against the truth. Dropping the records forfeits data but asserts nothing false. COST: removes ~5384 records from the candidate pool, of which ~370 would otherwise have been kept (mostly as AF). AF falls from 3107 to roughly 2741 valid records; LVH is essentially unchanged. TO ACCEPT IT AS LVH once a clinician confirms the code, set: maps_to: LVH status: ACCEPT which raises Chapman LVH from 645 to ~6027 and total LVH to ~8159.

*** NAMING TRAP: the acronym "AF" in this dataset means ATRIAL FLUTTER, not atrial fibrillation. *** 8036 records. Mapping this acronym to CardioSentry AF would inject 8036 flutter ECGs into the AF class -- more than four times the true AF count -- and is explicitly forbidden by the project rules. Atrial fibrillation is 164889003.
